passage:
A riverside town created an app that sent flood warnings to residents. It used rain data, river levels, and reports from local officials.
During a storm, the app warned people in low areas to move cars and prepare emergency bags. Many did so before the water rose.
However, some older residents did not use smartphones. Volunteers called them directly and knocked on doors.
The town learned that technology can send information quickly, but it cannot reach everyone by itself.
A good warning system uses many paths. In danger, the best message is the one that actually reaches the person who needs it.
